title: Semantic surface variants and button press contrast matrix
creator: Sana Patel
description: Problem: Our current dark-mode token mapping creates inconsistent perceived contrast when buttons are pressed and when dense table rows use elevated surfaces. This causes micro-regressions in accessibility audits and visual friction for enterprise brand themes. Objective: Define a compact, semantic set of surface variants (surface-0 through surface-5) and produce a button press contrast matrix that guarantees minimum contrast in all brand themes (primary, accent, neutral) across light/dark modes and compact density. Deliver a tokens spec, Figma library updates, component override guidance, and a dev-ready PR with implementation notes.
acceptance_criteria: Create a token spec with semantic surface variants and clear mapping rules for brand themes
Button press states (hover/active/focus) meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast thresholds in both light and dark across primary/neurtal/accent brand skins
Dense table rows using elevated surfaces preserve text and interactive affordance contrast at <32px row heights
Figma component library updated and annotated with token usage examples for each surface variant
Engineering PR with runtime mapping logic and backwards-compatible fallbacks merged to main or staged for release
design_notes: Introduce semantic tokens: surface-0..surface-5, interactive-1..interactive-3, accent-overlay to decouple brand hue from elevation
Use perceptual contrast targets (contrast ratio + luminance delta) rather than raw token deltas to ensure consistent appearance across brand saturations
Prototype two mapping algorithms: linear interpolation from base brand color and perceptual delta clamping. Leaning toward clamping for predictable edge cases with saturated brands
Button press states defined as modified overlay blends (multiply + alpha) layered on semantic surfaces to preserve depth cues without relying on pure darkening
Table density: introduce 'compact-surface' tokens derived from surface-1 but with enforced text contrast and subtle divider height increase for tactile affordance
decisions: Adopt semantic surface tokens (surface-0..surface-5) rather than per-component bespoke colors to reduce drift
Button press visual model will use an overlay blend with specified alpha values per surface level instead of fixed darker color tokens
Fallback rules: if brand mapping produces <3:1 contrast for non-critical microcopy, escalate to design review; for critical UI text enforce >=4.5:1
Charts with filled areas will use accent-overlay with controlled saturation; stroke-only charts remain on surface to avoid contrast conflicts
tradeoffs: Overlay blending provides better consistency across brands but requires runtime blend support (increases initial implementation complexity)
Stricter contrast enforcement reduces latitude for highly saturated brand themes; some brands will require neutralizing steps
Compact table surface constraints may slightly increase token surface count but improves accessibility and reduces ad-hoc overrides downstream
